description: JVM modules, imports, and exports slice (ISSUE-0096). JVM-only multi-module fixtures: each fixture writes its 'modules' (relative .deal source paths → DEAL source) plus 'entry' under a temp project root and runs the real whole-project pipeline — CompilationOrchestrator with Backend.JVM (module discovery, signature extraction, dependency ordering, name resolution, type checking, per-module JvmBackend codegen) → javac over every emitted .java artifact plus a runner class → java executing the emitted artifacts (the harness fails a fixture whose parser/checker/module-discovery yields no compile, whose codegen leaves no artifact, or whose JVM execution is bypassed). Covered forms: namespace imports (import * as alias from "...") of compiled project modules, exported functions consumed through imported direct calls (alias.fn(args) → a static call on the imported module's emitted class), imported calls at module level (load time) and inside function bodies, transitive import chains (depth-first load order), unused imports still running the imported module's load-time side effects, same-basename modules in different directories deriving isolated class names, multiple imports of same-named exports through distinct aliases, imported null-returning (void) calls, imported self-recursion, argument evaluation order with hoisted side effects across the module boundary, and three frontend compile-error gates rejected before any backend (E2004 missing export, E3009 arity mismatch, E5003 return-type mismatch in an imported module).

tests.name: jvm-mod-imported-direct-call
tests.description: A namespace import's exported function is called directly from the entry module: lib.add(2, 3) computes 5 through a static call on the imported module's emitted class

modules.lib.deal: export function add(a: int, b: int): int { return a + b; }
modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): int { return lib.add(2, 3); }

tests.name: jvm-mod-export-signatures
tests.description: Multiple exported functions with mixed signatures (boolean + string params, string returns) are consumed through the alias: pick selects the branch string and wrap decorates it

modules.lib.deal:
export function pick(flag: boolean, yes: string, no: string): string { if (flag) { return yes; } return no; }
export function wrap(s: string): string { return "[" + s + "]"; }

tests.name: jvm-mod-nested-module-calls
tests.description: An imported module's exported function internally calls its own non-exported function: outer(3, 4) = double(3) + double(4) = 14

modules.lib.deal:
function double(x: int): int { return x * 2; }
export function outer(a: int, b: int): int { return double(a) + double(b); }
modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): int { return lib.outer(3, 4); }

tests.name: jvm-mod-imported-recursion
tests.description: An imported exported function recurses on itself inside its own module: lib.fact(6) computes 720 across the module boundary

modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): int { return lib.fact(6); }

tests.name: jvm-mod-imported-void-call
tests.description: An imported null-returning exported function is called from the entry function body: the void call hoists into a pre-statement and its console output is observable

modules.lib.deal:
import * as console from "std/console"
export function announce(msg: string): null { console.log(msg); }
modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): null { lib.announce("from-lib"); }

tests.name: jvm-mod-import-load-time-order
tests.description: The import statement runs the imported module's load-time statements where it appears (depth-first, before the importing module's later load-time statements): lib-load, then main-load, then the called export prints ping

tests.name: jvm-mod-unused-import-side-effect
tests.description: An imported-but-unused alias still runs the imported module's load-time side effects (LuaJIT runs require for the import regardless of use): lib-initialized prints even though the alias is never referenced

modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): int { return 1; }

tests.name: jvm-mod-transitive-import
tests.description: A transitive import chain initializes depth-first in import order (c-load, b-load, main-load) and b's exported plus() calls c's exported base() across the b→c module boundary: plus(5) = 10 + 5 = 15

tests.name: jvm-mod-class-name-isolation
tests.description: Two modules with the same basename in different directories derive isolated class names (a/calc → ACalc, b/calc → BCalc): each defines its own same-named export compute(), and the entry calls both through distinct aliases — aCalc.compute() * 10 + bCalc.compute() = 12

tests.name: jvm-mod-load-time-imported-call
tests.description: An imported direct call at module level (load time) feeds a module field initializer: base = lib.value() = 40, then run() returns base + 2 = 42

tests.name: jvm-mod-imported-strings-while
tests.description: An imported exported function uses a while loop and string concatenation inside its own module: lib.repeat("ab", 3) returns "ababab" through the module boundary

modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): string { return lib.repeat("ab", 3); }

tests.name: jvm-mod-imported-arg-order
tests.description: Left-to-right argument evaluation with hoisted null-typed side effects holds across the module boundary: the two console.log arguments run first then second before the imported pair() call returns 7

modules.lib.deal: export function pair(x: null, y: null): int { return 7; }

tests.name: jvm-mod-multiple-imports
tests.description: Two imports whose exported function names are identical stay distinct through their aliases: left.value() + right.value() = 30 + 12 = 42

tests.name: jvm-mod-missing-export
tests.description: Frontend compile-error gate (E2004): the entry module calls lib.missing(), which the imported module does not export — the real orchestrator frontend rejects the project before any backend, and no .java artifact is written

modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): int { return lib.missing(1); }

tests.name: jvm-mod-imported-arity-mismatch
tests.description: Frontend compile-error gate (E3009): the entry module calls the imported two-parameter lib.add() with one argument — the real orchestrator frontend rejects the project before any backend, and no .java artifact is written

modules.lib.deal: export function add(a: int, b: int): int { return a + b; }
modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): int { return lib.add(1); }

tests.name: jvm-mod-imported-type-error
tests.description: Frontend compile-error gate (E5003): the IMPORTED module itself has a return-type error (broken(): int returns a string) — the real orchestrator frontend type-checks lib.deal and rejects the project before any backend, and no .java artifact is written

modules.lib.deal: export function broken(): int { return "not an int"; }
modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): int { return lib.broken(); }
